blocks.text: Carboxylic acids can be prepared by the following methods.
a) Oxidation of primary alcohols and aldehydes
Carboxylic acids are prepared by the oxidation of primary alcohols and aldehydes. The starting material is refluxed with excess of either acidified KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇.

blocks.alt: Two equations with K2Cr2O7/dil. H2SO4 over the arrow and Heat under it. Ethanol, CH3-CH2-OH, + 2[O] gives ethanoic acid, CH3-C(=O)-OH, + H2O. Ethanal, CH3-C(=O)-H, + [O] gives ethanoic acid.
blocks.caption: a) Oxidation of ethanol and ethanal to ethanoic acid (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 108).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed equation for ethanal also has '+ H₂O' on the right, so it is not balanced; it is CH₃CHO + [O] → CH₃COOH, as drawn above.
Alkane nitriles can be directly hydrolysed to carboxylic acids in acidic medium. In alkaline hydrolyses, they first produce salts of carboxylic acids, which yield carboxylic acids on acidification.

blocks.alt: Three equations. CH3-CN + 2H2O + HCl -> CH3-C(=O)-OH + NH4Cl. CH3-CN + H2O + NaOH -> CH3-C(=O)-O-Na+ + NH3 (gas). CH3-C(=O)-O-Na+ + HCl -> CH3-C(=O)-OH + NaCl.
blocks.caption: b) Hydrolysis of ethanenitrile in acid and in alkali, and acidification of the salt (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 109).

blocks.text: When an ester is refluxed with either dilute acid or dilute alkali, the ester is hydrolyzed to carboxylic acid or carboxylate ion.

blocks.alt: Three equations. Ethyl ethanoate, CH3-C(=O)-O-CH2-CH3, + H2O(l), with H3O+ over equilibrium arrows, gives CH3-C(=O)-OH + CH3-CH2-OH. Ethyl ethanoate + NaOH(aq) gives CH3-C(=O)-O-Na+ + CH3-CH2-OH; an arrow labelled 'Bond breaks' points at the bond between the C=O carbon and the O. CH3-C(=O)-O-Na+ + HCl gives CH3-C(=O)-OH + NaCl.
blocks.caption: c) Hydrolysis of ethyl ethanoate in acid and in alkali, and acidification of the salt (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 109).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed alkaline hydrolysis uses equilibrium arrows; with NaOH the acid formed becomes its salt and the reaction goes to completion, so a one-way arrow is drawn.
d) Preparation of benzenecarboxylic acid (Benzoic acid)
Methyl benzene is readily oxidized by acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇ to benzoic acid.

blocks.alt: Methylbenzene (a benzene ring with CH3) + 3[O], with KMnO4 over the arrow and dil. H2SO4; Heat under it, gives benzene carboxylic acid (a benzene ring with COOH) + H2O.
blocks.caption: d) Oxidation of methylbenzene to benzenecarboxylic acid (benzoic acid) (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 109).
